paragraphs: Here's what this chapter is really showing us, friend. Solomon has officials, governors, oxen and 12,000 horses, and then the text says this: "God gave Solomon wisdom, exceedingly deep insight, and understanding beyond measure" (1 Kings 4:29). Of everything in that long list, this is the part the text says God gave. I've baked a LOT of cookies, and I can tell you that a fancy oven means nothing if you don't know what you're doing.

Now look at the life of the people in this chapter. Judah and Israel "dwelt securely from Dan to Beersheba, each man under his own vine and his own fig tree" (1 Kings 4:25). Solomon's wisdom wasn't a trophy to keep on a shelf, because he composed three thousand proverbs and his songs numbered a thousand and five (1 Kings 4:32), and "men of all nations came to listen to Solomon's wisdom" (1 Kings 4:34). Wisdom that God gives is meant to be shared.

So here's the takeaway for you, baker. Wisdom is a gift God gives, and He can give it to a king or to a worn-out stamper from the back of a junk drawer. Every time you open the Word, you're sitting where those nations sat, listening and learning. And I'll tell you what, that's a better spot than any seat at Solomon's table.
